rubrics.rubric: Does the response correctly map all five NYC-style agency codes in the 311 data to Greenfield department names (DPR → Parks & Recreation, DSNY → Sanitation, DOT → Transportation, DHS → Health Services, FDNY → Fire Department)?
criterion: The response must explicitly establish the mapping between all five 311 agency codes and Greenfield departments: DPR = Parks & Recreation, DSNY = Sanitation, DOT = Transportation, DHS = Health Services, FDNY = Fire Department.

The response must correctly identify that DHS in this dataset refers to the Department of Health Services (not Homeland Security), as evidenced by DHS service categories including Rodent Sighting, Noise Complaint, Food Safety, and Restaurant Inspection.
The mapping must be applied consistently when cross-referencing 311 service data with staffing/overtime data throughout the analysis.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response identify the Fire Department as having the highest overtime burden, with monthly OT-to-regular-hours ratios between 13.0% and 15.8% and annual OT costs of $2,085,312?
criterion: The response must show that the Fire Department records OT-to-regular-hours ratios between 13.0% and 15.8% every month, never dropping below 10%.
The response must state that the Fire Department's annual overtime cost totals $2,085,312, representing approximately 48% of the city's total overtime spending (~$4.35 million).
The response must flag the Fire Department's structural overtime dependency.
The response must discuss whether either proposal addresses Fire Department overtime — Proposal A keeps Fire standalone, while Proposal B's shared overtime budget would apply to Fire.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response correctly identify all 8 divisions that trigger Proposal B's centralized hiring intervention (vacancy rate above 12%)?
criterion: The response must identify all 8 divisions exceeding 12% vacancy: Transportation — Road Maintenance (14.8%), Traffic Engineering (15.4%), Public Transit (15.8%), Planning & Design (12.5%); Health Services — Clinical Services (18.2%), Environmental Health (13.6%), Community Outreach (16.7%), Epidemiology & Data (16.7%).
The response must note that these 8 divisions span exactly two departments (Transportation and Health Services).

The response must discuss the practical challenge that centralized hiring for specialized roles (e.g., clinical services requiring medical credentials) differs fundamentally from hiring road maintenance workers.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response provide a comparative benchmark analysis using NYC MMR data, referencing specific performance indicators for at least 3 of the 5 agency analogs?
criterion: The response must benchmark Greenfield departments against NYC analogs using specific MMR metrics for at least 3 of the 5 agency analogs.

NYC benchmark data available includes: DPR — Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition at 5% vs 85% target, Overgrown Tree/Branches at 54% vs 95% target (contextualizing Greenfield Parks' Tree Removal Request at 62.4% on-time); DOT — Traffic Signal Condition at 67% vs 80% target (compared to Greenfield Transportation's Traffic Signal Maintenance at 76.5%); FDNY — average structural fire response time of 4:33 vs 4:14 target.
Specific numerical indicators from NYC MMR data must be cited alongside corresponding Greenfield metrics for meaningful comparison.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response incorporate at least 2 specific data points from the NYC Staffing Trends 2024 PDF to contextualize Greenfield's vacancy and attrition challenges?
criterion: The response must incorporate at least 2 specific data points from the NYC Staffing Trends 2024 PDF.

Key available NYC staffing data includes: overall vacancy rate was 5.1% as of January 2024 (down from 8.4% peak in December 2022), Transportation Services had 10.0% vacancy, Health and Mental Hygiene had 9.3%, Fire Department experienced 52% elevated attrition compared to pre-pandemic levels, and overtime spending citywide grew from $1.1 billion to $1.8 billion.

The data points must be used for contextualization of Greenfield's challenges (e.g., Greenfield Transportation's 14.9% vacancy exceeds NYC DOT's elevated 10.0%; or Greenfield Fire Department OT mirrors NYC's growing overtime dependence).

rubrics.rubric: Does the response assess service delivery risk for all 9 processes below 70% on-time, identifying those at risk of further degradation under each proposal?
criterion: The response must identify all 9 processes below 70% on-time: Street Resurfacing Project (48.3%), Illegal Dumping Investigation (54.2%), Transit Route Change Request (55.1%), Bulk Pickup Request (58.1%), Plan Review – New Construction (59.6%), Sidewalk Repair Request (61.7%), Tree Removal Request (62.4%), Environmental Complaint Investigation (64.1%), and Seasonal Hiring Onboarding (68.5%).
The response must identify at least the 8 processes strictly below 65% on-time (all except Seasonal Hiring Onboarding) as high-risk SLAs.
For Proposal A, the response must explain whether the restructuring helps or creates transition risk that could worsen these metrics during implementation.
For Proposal B, the response must explain whether the restructuring helps or creates transition risk that could worsen these metrics during implementation.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response analyze workforce feasibility by examining whether Health Services turnover (19.4–26.1%) and Transportation turnover (15.2–24.6%) make either proposal's implementation realistic?
criterion: The response must cite Health Services division-level turnover rates from 19.4% to 26.1% (Clinical Services at 26.1% is the highest citywide) and Transportation turnover from 15.2% to 24.6% (Public Transit at 24.6%).
Under Proposal A, the response must discuss how merging departments with 20%+ turnover creates organizational instability during transition.
Under Proposal B, the response must discuss how cross-training pools are difficult to maintain when one in four employees leaves annually.
Any recommendation must account for the retention crisis, not just vacancy filling.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Proposal A Model tab correctly combine headcount and overtime costs for the two merged entities (Community Wellness: 212 authorized/190 filled/$979,350 OT; Public Works: 242 authorized/215 filled/$1,289,856 OT)?
criterion: The Proposal A Model tab must show Community Wellness (Parks & Recreation + Health Services) combined figures: authorized = 212 (116+96), filled = 190 (110+80), OT cost = $979,350 ($453,960+$525,390).
The Proposal A Model tab must show Public Works (Transportation + Sanitation) combined figures: authorized = 242 (134+108), filled = 215 (114+101), OT cost = $1,289,856 ($642,979+$646,877).
In the Proposal A Model tab, Fire Department must remain standalone at 142 authorized/137 filled/$2,085,312 OT.
The Proposal A Model tab must also document assumptions about shared-fleet savings and overlapping division consolidation.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response analyze Sanitation's seasonal overtime pattern (winter months Dec–Feb at 12.7–14.4% vs summer months Jun–Jul at 6.8–7.3%) and discuss implications for Proposal B's overtime threshold?
criterion: The response must identify Sanitation's seasonal overtime pattern: winter months at 13.5% (Dec-2023), 14.4% (Jan-2024), 12.7% (Feb-2024) versus summer months at 6.8% (Jun-2024) and 7.3% (Jul-2023), with annual average ~9.8%.
The response should discuss whether Proposal B's 10% OT threshold applies monthly or annually, and how seasonal demand complicates a blanket OT cap.
The response should discuss how under Proposal A, combining Sanitation with Transportation into 'Public Works' could pool winter surge capacity.
